cells.tense: Right now you are sitting where feeling with someone and staying yourself are the same act.
cells.act: go where the feeling is already pulling
cells.ask: Notice who your attention keeps drifting toward, and today let that draw you one step closer — a call made, a plan set, a question spoken. Nothing pushed. Go where the feeling goes.
cells.core: Being with someone and feeling your way forward turn out not to be two jobs. You lean toward a person without needing to see where it leads; enough light arrives for the next step. When things are unclear, you notice that. But the way a feeling moves you toward someone is real information, and you have been treating it that way — it comes from what you have already lived through, not from what you wish were so. So the pull can be trusted. That is worth saying plainly, because it usually gets called being indecisive. It is not. It is what keeps you honest in a room with someone and still open to what they show you next.
cells.sheetLine: The pull toward someone is information, not fog.
cells.verb: moving through what is not clear yet without forcing the road
cells.place: beside someone, feeling with them while you stay yourself

cells.tense: Soon the room will keep being smaller than the picture you are already painting of it.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Cook a meal, water a plant, send a message — then walk away from it. No checking what came back, no adding to it. Let it be done and be gone.
cells.core: Beside someone, the shape of what this is becoming is already clear to you. You can see the whole arc, and mostly you are right, which is the trouble. A living person is smaller than the dream of where they fit, and your care has started reaching past them to the version ahead. Nothing cruel sits in that; it is wanting, running ahead of talk. So the correction is not less care. It is care that stops steering. Let the other person be someone whose words come slower than your imagining, which is not the same as giving up what you see. Both are real — the vision, and the one who has not yet filled it in.

cells.tense: You are no longer walking through that door, but you still stand facing it.
cells.act: sit with not knowing for ten minutes instead of filling it
cells.ask: Pick a relationship you can't read, and sit with it ten minutes. No theory, no sorting it out. Not knowing is the work. When the time is up, stand and go on.
cells.core: With people, the direct read has gone quiet. You get there by arguing now — what is probably going on, what to say next — and the argument is doing the work the first look used to do. What is left is careful and a little airless. Nothing has to be fixed in your heart tonight. But one read can come back, in one room, with one person, if you let not-knowing sit there a few minutes without rushing it. It will not feel like a technique. It will feel like the first thing you knew — something you can act on, or keep, no more than that.
cells.sheetLine: You ask your way to what you used to just see.

cells.tense: You are shaping something right now you have not yet owned as yours.
cells.act: refine one piece by repeating it
cells.ask: Take a passage, a chord, a route you walk, and repeat it today exactly as it was — same words, same pace. Then again tomorrow. The sameness is the point.
cells.core: There is a picture of where this is going with someone, and you did not decide to make it. It arrived, and you have been following it — small moves, half-echoes of earlier versions of the same thing — while calling it circumstance. It is not a fault. It is a hand that has not signed its own canvas, and the fix is not insight. It is something done alone, the same plain way, until the shape becomes obvious because it kept showing up. From there you can decide what to do with the person. The dream stops running you the moment you see it was yours.
cells.sheetLine: You are dreaming a direction and calling it circumstance.
